title: Carry prior result and change scope into retry readings; refuse
summary: For a retried or follow-up job, the reader's brief must always state the previous attempt's result (verdict, findings, end state) and the allowed change scope (deliverables and out-of-scope). A new check then refuses any reading that omits either. Audience: the reader agent and the verifier. Root cause: the brief carries these only partly and nothing enforces the reading to use them.

defaults_applied.how: New failing-then-passing tests plus cargo test and clippy criteria.
The criteria require naming the root cause and adding a mechanism check, not only prompt text.
A code check enforces the rule instead of prose only.
The tests exercise the brief output and the refusal.
The criteria check that a reading omitting the result or scope is refused.
One focused change in the reading and brief code.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Existing machinery (EarlierAttempt in athena-context briefs.rs, earlier_attempt/referenced_jobs in athena-core reading.rs) already carries findings, reading criteria and deliverables; the gap is the end state and out-of-scope (change scope) for retries and follow-ups, and that no check refuses a reading that ignores them. I did not see the actual introspection records, which are absent.

The queued item reading-omits-prior-verifier-finding-or-end-state is in records/, which I cannot read. I assume it overlaps on the prior finding and end-state half. This job covers it, adds the scope half and the refusal check, and names the overlap in its summary and the changelog; it does not edit the queue.
The check lives where a reading is accepted after read_for in athena-core and fails the reading with a clear message, so the reader is asked again within the existing revision loop.

A reading 'leaves out' the prior result if it neither addresses the earlier findings or end state in its summary, assumptions or criteria, nor states why they no longer apply. A deterministic check can test this by comparing the reading's text and criteria against the carried findings, deliverables and out-of-scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: The reader brief for a retry (try again on <job>) and for a follow-up job that names an earlier job includes a section with the previous attempt's result (verdict, findings or outcome reason, end state) and the allowed change scope (deliverable paths and out-of-scope items), with the scope present even if the earlier reading had none.

A new check function in athena-core refuses a reading for a retried or follow-up job that does not reflect the prior result or does not state the change scope, returning an error that names which of the two is missing. It does not apply to a first-attempt job.

The change summary or CHANGELOG states the root cause (the brief and the acceptance of a reading did not require the prior result and scope) and states the overlap with reading-omits-prior-verifier-finding-or-end-state: what it covers and what is left.

New unit tests in crates/athena-context and crates/athena-core fail on the pre-change code and pass after. They cover the brief containing the result and scope, a reading missing the result refused, a reading missing the scope refused, a complete reading accepted, and a first attempt unaffected. Run `cargo test` and compare with the base.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass from the repository root with no new warnings.

out_of_scope: Editing or closing the queued item reading-omits-prior-verifier-finding-or-end-state (records/ is not changed)
Changing the verifier, producer or landing behavior
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass odds than the reference. The check has to judge free-text readings against carried context, and the overlap with a queued item I cannot see is an extra risk.
urgent_reason: It cuts failed and rejected retries, which come from readings that ignore the previous result and scope. The seven introspections record this as the repeated cause.
hard_reason: It adds a gate that refuses readings, and that gate decides which jobs proceed.
